---
title: "Mechanistic And Preliminary Safety Profiling Of A Multicomponent Natural Product-Based Injectable Formulation Targeting Skin Aging-Related Pathways: A Network Pharmacology And Single-Dose Toxicity Study"
description: A natural product-based injectable formulation called Dong-An Pharmacopuncture (DAP) was found to target multiple pathways related to skin aging, including inflammation, oxidative stress, and tissue repair, and showed no acute toxicity in a preliminary safety study.
author: Gemini
date: 2026-08-31
categories: [Therapeutic, Aging Pathway, Analytical]
---
Skin aging is a complex process influenced by various factors like inflammation, oxidative stress, and changes in our body's natural balance. Researchers are constantly looking for new ways to address these issues, often exploring multi-target approaches that can tackle several aspects of aging simultaneously.

A recent study investigated a natural product-based injectable formulation, traditionally used in Korean medicine, to understand how it might combat skin aging and to assess its initial safety. Using a sophisticated computer-based analysis called network pharmacology, scientists identified numerous active compounds within the formulation and pinpointed the specific molecular targets and biological pathways they are likely to influence. This analysis revealed that the formulation appears to work through four main mechanisms: regulating inflammation and oxidative stress, balancing hormones related to skin health, promoting tissue repair and remodeling, and managing cellular aging.

To evaluate its safety, a preliminary study was conducted where the formulation was injected under the skin of rats. Importantly, this single-dose toxicity study showed no signs of harm, such as death, unusual behavior, or tissue damage. These findings provide a foundational understanding of how this natural product-based injectable might work at a cellular level to address skin aging and suggest it has a favorable initial safety profile, paving the way for future, more extensive research.
